description.value: A vehicle-accessible group campsite set in Goldstream Provincial Park's cathedral old-growth of 600-year-old Douglas firs, just 16 km from Victoria; the annual chum salmon spawning run draws bald eagles and thousands of visitors each autumn. Group sites carry a minimum charge for 15 adults, making them cost-effective only for larger parties.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies this as a group campsite within Goldstream Provincial Park, with the BC Parks website confirmed reachable and corroborating an active, vehicle-accessible campground 16km from Victoria. The website explicitly mentions picnic shelters, a summer concession, and group site reservations via camping.bcparks.ca — these are the primary evidence sources for amenity values. No bike-specific amenities (hiker/biker sites, showers, pump, etc.) are mentioned anywhere on the website.
concerns: This is a group-only campsite — BC Parks group camping policy requires a minimum charge for 15 adults, making it impractical for solo or small cycling parties.
No address or phone number present in OSM record.
Summer concession availability is seasonal; no year-round food source confirmed on site.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a dedicated group campsite requiring a minimum booking for 15 adults (or 12 youth via a qualifying organization), which makes it unsuitable for individual or small-party touring cyclists; it warrants review to determine whether WWC should list group-only sites.
enrichment_extras.notes: The park itself has vehicle-accessible individual campsites in addition to group sites, but this specific OSM record maps only the Goldminer (Lower) group site. A separate OSM record for the general Goldstream campground may be more appropriate for individual touring cyclists.
